findings.title: Embedded-post author color inverted for light themes
findings.body: The embedded-post username link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This change sets the light-theme branch to 70% and the dark-theme branch to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). Light themes therefore render that name much lighter than before, and dark themes get a 30%-lightness secondary (a dark gray on a dark background) instead of the complementary 70%. The author name in expanded replies will lose the intended contrast in both schemes. Keep $lightness: 30% on $primary and use $lightness: 70% on $secondary.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: Topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses 50% for both branches, matching the h4 rule below it rather than the original value. Desktop topic-map h3 in this same PR correctly becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)). On mobile, light-theme map headings will be washed out relative to the previous design and to desktop, and dark themes will not get the lighter complementary secondary. Restore 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message-length light and dark branches are swapped
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new rule uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) in the light branch and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) in the dark branch. Desktop modal.scss in this PR keeps 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. Mobile light themes will show a much darker hint than before, and dark themes will lighten $secondary by 70% instead of 30%, so the hint will not match desktop or the previous light-theme color. Swap the percentages back to 70% / 30%.

findings.title: Group member name lightness raised from 30% to 50%
findings.body: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), distinct from the adjacent .title at 50%. The new color uses 50% for both the light $primary branch and the dark $secondary branch, so the name collapses to the same color as the title. Light themes lose that hierarchy, and dark themes get a 50%-lightness secondary instead of the complementary 70%. Use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

findings.title: Mobile group member name lightness raised from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same mistake as desktop user.scss: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title. Light-theme names become lighter than before and no longer differ from titles; dark themes do not get the 70% secondary complement of the original 30%. Restore 30% on $primary and 70% on $secondary.

findings.title: Category badge notification still scales $primary only
findings.body: In the same file, topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in dark-light-choose so dark themes scale $secondary. .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification is still color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) on a transparent background. On a dark scheme $primary is already the light text color, so this pushes the count further toward white and leaves the exact dark-theme failure this PR is fixing. Wrap it as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)).
